title: Enquiring About a Flat to Rent

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Good afternoon, Hartley Lettings, Fiona speaking. How can I help?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Oh, hi, yes. I saw an advert on your website for a one-bedroom flat, and I wanted to find out a bit more about it, and maybe arrange a viewing.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Of course. Do you happen to have the reference number? It's usually at the top of the listing.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Um, let me just look... yes, it's H L, then four oh seven. Sorry, no, four seven oh.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: H L four seven oh, lovely. That's the flat on Carlton Road, the one above the bakery. Before we go any further, can I take your name?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Sure. It's Marcus Delaney. That's D, E, L, A, N, E, Y.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Thanks, Marcus. And what's the best number to reach you on?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: My mobile is best. It's oh seven seven eight one, five five two, oh three nine.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Great, I've got that. So, what would you like to know about the flat?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Well, the advert said the rent was eight hundred and fifty pounds a month. Is that right? It seemed quite reasonable for the area.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Ah, that was the old price, actually. The landlord put it up last week, so it's now eight hundred and ninety-five a month. I'm sorry, the website hasn't been updated yet.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Oh, right. Does that include any bills?

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Water is included, but you'd pay for electricity and the internet yourself. And council tax as well, of course.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: OK. And is it furnished?

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: It's partly furnished. There's a sofa, a bed and a wardrobe, but no desk or dining table, so you might need to bring your own.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: That's fine, I've got a desk. What about the deposit? How much is that?

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: The deposit is equal to five weeks' rent. It's held in a government protection scheme, so you get it back at the end as long as there's no damage.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Five weeks. OK. And what's the minimum contract? I'm hoping to stay at least a year.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: The landlord asks for a minimum of six months, and after that it rolls on month by month. Or you can sign for twelve months from the start, if you'd prefer.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Twelve sounds better for me. Oh, I should mention, I cycle to work. Is there anywhere to keep a bike?

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: There isn't a garage, I'm afraid, but there's a locked shed in the back garden that the tenants share. Most people keep their bikes in there.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Perfect. And how far is it from the station?

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: It's about a ten-minute walk to Northgate station. That's N, O, R, T, H, G, A, T, E. And the number twelve bus stops right outside.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Great. So when would it be available?

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: The current tenant moves out at the end of this month, so it would be free from the third of November. Actually, hang on... there's a note here. The landlord wants a few days to repaint the kitchen, so let's say the seventh of November, to be safe.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: The seventh is fine. Could I come and see it before then?

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Certainly. I've got Thursday at half past five, or Saturday morning at ten.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Thursday's tricky, I don't finish work till six. Saturday at ten would be ideal.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Saturday at ten it is. Just so you know, we'll also need a reference, either from your current landlord or from your employer, before you can sign anything.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: My employer would be easier, I think. I've only been renting from my current landlord for a few months, so he doesn't really know me.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: That's no problem. Shall I email you the application form? What's your email address?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: It's marcus dot d at fastmail dot com. Hmm, no, actually, use my work one. It's m dot delaney at brightwave dot co dot uk.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Lovely, I'll send it this afternoon. And when you arrive on Saturday, the entrance is at the side of the bakery, not the front. Look for a blue door.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Blue door, got it. Thanks very much, Fiona.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: You're welcome, Marcus. See you on Saturday.

groups.instructions: Complete the form below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
groups.template:

Example: Reference number: HL470

- Location of flat: {{1}} Road (above a bakery)
- Caller's name: Marcus {{2}}
- Rent: £{{3}} per month
- Bills included in rent: {{4}} only
- Deposit: {{5}} weeks' rent
- Bicycle storage: in a shared {{6}} in the back garden
- Nearest station: {{7}} (10-minute walk)
- Available from: {{8}} November
- Viewing arranged for: {{9}} at 10 a.m.

questions.explanation: The agent identifies the listing as 'the flat on Carlton Road, the one above the bakery'.
The advert said 850, but the agent corrects this: the landlord raised the rent to 895 a month. 850 is a distractor.
'Water is included'; electricity, internet and council tax are paid separately.
'The deposit is equal to five weeks' rent.'
There is no garage (distractor), but there is 'a locked shed in the back garden that the tenants share'.
The agent names and spells Northgate station, a ten-minute walk away.
The agent first says the third, then corrects it to the seventh because the kitchen needs repainting.
Thursday at 5.30 is rejected because Marcus works until six; he chooses Saturday at ten.
The reference can come from the landlord or the employer; Marcus says his employer would be easier.
